Comment of Nancy Piotrowski in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15424-000
Submission Date: 11/2/2026

documents.text:
Nancy Piotrowski, Vallejo, CA.
Nancy A. Piotrowski, Ph.D. <piotrowskiconsultation@gmail.com>
	
2:10 PM (17 minutes ago)
	

To:

Debbie-Anne A. Reese, Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First Street, NE
Washington, DC 20426
OPP@ferc.gov

RE: 
LETTER OF PROTEST
DEEPGREEN HOLDINGS LLC
DOCKET #P-15424-000


My name is Nancy A. Piotrowski, Ph.D., and I am a resident of Vallejo, California. I am writing today to register my OPPOSITION to the permit approved on 8/20/26 to DEEPGREEN HOLDINGS LLC for the WESTERN PASSAGE SUBSEA COMPUTER AND INFRASTRUCTURE HUB.  I STRONGLY OPPOSE the project progressing.

I oppose this project because it is proposed to be done in environmentally sensitive areas where it creates threats to wildlife, some of which are already at risk or endangered, as well as local ecosystems, including local communities that depend on maritime economies.  Further, the work is proposed in areas where ocean current patterns that have the potential to affect climate are already  stressed and absorbing increased heat from global warming.  On the Atlantic side we have issues related to AMOC [e.g.Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation] and on the Pacific side, we have issues related to stresses in the Bering Sea (e.g., record high temperatures as the sea bottom, record losses of sea ice, acidification of ocean water, coastal erosion). I find the locations of the proposed work very troubling, on a global scale, particularly given the already known issues affecting and threatening further problems with circulating ocean currents in the Atlantic and the impact of ocean warming affecting regions near the Bering Sea. 

While the proponents of the project may see their proposed work as a solution to promote data center development, the locations are too sensitive for all the reasons noted.  Adding more warming to a warming ocean and sea are not wise.   In fact, given what we have already seen related to climate change and ocean warming, I consider the proposed work myopic and reckless.  The prospective benefit is not worth the known costs and prospective risks and further costs. The harms and prospective costs likewise are magnified considering the size of the longer term proposed work and potential disruption/destruction zones created proximal to the work, and the rippling impact out to the ecosystem as a whole.  
It's too big of a gamble - and these areas already need our protection, not more threat.


Please know I am submitting these comments today because I only learned about the proposed work today.  I had seen no national or other news coverage of these issues in my community in written, online, or televised news coverage until I learned about it today on LinkedIn. 

Thank you for your consideration of these comments.

Sincerely,

Nancy A. Piotrowski, Ph.D.
